bc_fantasyland.blurb: Fantasyland is a bench of boulders above Arrow Lake in the West Kootenay of British Columbia, with views across the lake. Every climb is a boulder problem, and the density is high. Most sit between V1 and V4, with a good number up to V8 and a couple at V10. Borderlands holds the most climbs, followed by Trekkie, Comic, Witchcraft & Wizardry and Middle Earth. Around Arrow Lake the rock is a compact gneiss with many features, the slopes face south, and conditions are generally dry from about March to November. Castlegar is roughly ten minutes from the Arrow Lake boulders.

ca_big_chief.blurb: Big Chief sits high on a ridge above Highway 89 in the Truckee River Canyon, in the Lake Tahoe area. Nearly every route is a bolted sport climb, and it has the highest concentration of sport climbing within or near the Tahoe Basin. Most routes fall at 5.10 and 5.11, with a solid group at 5.12 and a few easier and harder. The rock is volcanic, vertical to slightly overhanging with a few very steep sections, and the canyon as a whole holds many basalt formations. Mini Buttress, Three Towers Wall, Center Wall and Light Deprivation Buttress hold the most climbs. It is mainly a summer and fall destination, and most walls face southwest, so summer days can be very warm.

ca_way_lake.blurb: Way Lake is a boulder field at about 9,800 feet above Mammoth Lakes, in California's Eastern Sierra, with an alpine feel. It is reached on foot by the Emerald Lake trail and a climb to a plateau. The problems sit on good quality rock and cover the full range of grades: plenty from V0 to V5, a solid run from V6 to V9, and a few at V10 and V11. Of the Mammoth Lakes bouldering areas, Way Lake holds the most climbs. It splits into zones such as Lower Meadow Area, Crimp Ladder Area, Lower Talus Area and Middle Meadow.

co_leadville.blurb: Leadville gathers climbing areas around the Colorado town, which sits at about 10,200 feet; the boundaries between areas are blurry. It is a real mix: trad and sport lead, with alpine routes, a few boulders and top ropes, and some ice and mixed climbs. Most roped grades fall between 5.9 and 5.11. Camp Hale, north of Leadville and just east of US 24, holds the most climbs, a small sport spot with classics from 5.6 to 5.12b. Hell's Gate and Hagerman Pass is a granite area with both trad and sport climbing. Many crags are high, and the colder months make them difficult to climb.

co_satellite_boulders.blurb: Satellite Boulders sit at the base of the Second Flatiron in the North Flatirons of Boulder, Colorado, approached by trail from Chautauqua. Every climb is a boulder problem. V0 and V1 make up the largest share, with a spread of mid grades and a handful from V7 to V9. BBC Boulder holds the most climbs, then Base of 2nd Flatiron Boulders, The Wave Boulder, Dark Side Boulders and Sputnik Boulder. The North Flatirons are hard conglomerate sandstone. The best time to go is when there is no snow on the ground. Upper Satellite Boulders sit several hundred feet higher, in a drainage between the Second and Third Flatirons, where summers are cooler and little winter sun arrives.

id_dierkes_lake_bouldering.blurb: Dierkes Lake Bouldering is on the north shore of Dierkes Lake, just outside Twin Falls, in Idaho's Snake River Canyon area, with an approach of about five minutes. The rock is highly featured basalt, with huecos, pockets, jugs, crimps, pinches and slopers, and the boulders have flat, grassy landings. Every climb is a boulder problem, mostly V0 to V4 with a thinner tail up to V8. Kid Boulder Area holds the most climbs, then Stairs Left and Stairs Right, with Down Under Corridor Area and Greenroom Area behind. The area is a sun trap, good in fall, winter and spring, and very hot in summer.
